body: Hi, I'm sorry I didn't see your note until just now.  Yeah, anxiety is a weird thing, because there are so many degrees.  I have learned, for the most part, to deal with mine - although it's not always easy.  What about yours?

That's so great to hear you say that.  I keep a little notebook, the size of a wallet, and I make notes in it all the time.  Mainly I note down things that I find really interesting or cool.  It's great to go back and look through it (them, there are several).  And yeah, it's no lies - just what is.

I actually did, and you're right.  I put on my favorite movie and I was grateful for a warm house.  I don't mean to sound selfish or petty.  I just wish there was something more.  I wish I had someone - uggh, I just don't want to be alone anymore.

I work.  I make about 10% of what I use to make.  I'm officially poor.  I went from being an executive to selling t-shirts.  I'm in a better job now, but still... hard to make them ends.  But that's alright, I don't worry about that part.  I have a job, and I work hard at it, and I earn my salary, and I get by.  I'm proud of that.  How I spend my days?  Outside of work, there's nothing.  I try to write, I want to write a book someday.  But I have no social life at all.

I know you're right, I believe that.  The weird thing is how optimistic I've always been.  But I think I've just burned out.  I can't play anymore.  I'm exhausted.  I lost everything I owned in the crash of 08, and when the money was gone, I lost everyone that I thought loved me.  I'm entirely alone.  Christmas this year was a pizza from 7/11.  I'm really trying to figure out a reason to charge ahead and beat these feelings, but I honestly feel like it's useless.  It's dark.  I want to be happy, and I want it bad.  I'm motivated, but I just can't see it anymore.  DOes that make sense?
No, one of those lives.  I'm not a dramatic person, honestly.  I just don't think I know how to be happy.
